reasoning: Recent Maine polling in the last month shows Democrat Troy Jackson consistently leading Republican Sen. Susan Collins by low single digits, with all surveys within their margins of error but all favoring Jackson, suggesting a slight Democratic edge in the 2026 Senate race. Multiple polls (UNH, Fox News, Hart Research) and news write‑ups describe the contest as extremely close but with Jackson narrowly ahead, while no recent reputable source shows Collins clearly leading. Structurally, Maine is modestly Democratic-leaning (Cook PVI D+2), so taken together the current picture is a D+2–3 environment in the Senate race rather than a clear advantage for either side.

sources.name: Spectrum Local News (summary of UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: UNH Pine Tree State Poll found Troy Jackson at 49% and Susan Collins at 46% among likely general-election voters in Maine, describing the race as a statistical tie but with Jackson slightly ahead.

sources.name: The Hill (on UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: The Hill’s report on the University of New Hampshire poll notes Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46% among likely voters, calling it a slight lead in a hypothetical general-election matchup.

sources.name: Portland Press Herald (on UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: Portland Press Herald reports that 49% of likely voters would pick Jackson vs. 46% for Collins, stating Jackson has a slight edge though the race is close.

sources.name: Bangor Daily News (on Fox News Maine Senate poll)
sources.details: Bangor Daily News, summarizing a Fox News poll, reports Jackson leading Collins 48% to 46% among registered Maine voters, noting it as a slight edge in the U.S. Senate race.

sources.name: Political Wire (on Fox News Maine Senate poll)
sources.details: Political Wire summarizes a Fox News poll in Maine finding Jackson ahead of Collins 48% to 46%, emphasizing that the two‑point advantage is within the margin of error.

sources.name: Newsweek (on Fox News Maine Senate poll)
sources.details: Newsweek’s coverage of the Fox News poll reports Jackson at 48% and Collins at 46% in the 2026 Maine Senate race, describing the contest as increasingly competitive with Jackson holding a narrow lead.

sources.name: Newsweek (on Hart Research/Senate Majority PAC poll)
sources.details: Newsweek reports a Hart Research Associates poll sponsored by Senate Majority PAC showing Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45% among 802 likely voters, a four‑point advantage within the margin of error.

sources.name: The Maine Wire (on Hart Research/Senate Majority PAC poll)
sources.details: The Maine Wire describes the Hart Research poll commissioned by Senate Majority PAC, finding Jackson ahead of Collins 49% to 45% with 6% undecided, characterizing the race as close but with Jackson leading.

sources.name: WGME (on Hart Research/Senate Majority PAC poll)
sources.details: WGME local news reports that a Hart Research poll for Senate Majority PAC shows Jackson ahead 49% to 45%, noting that another new poll finds Democrat Troy Jackson holding a slight lead against Sen. Susan Collins.

sources.name: The Maine Wire (multi-poll summary: Fox News, UNH, Hart)
sources.details: The Maine Wire’s broader analysis of the race notes a Fox News poll showing Jackson 48% to 46%, a UNH poll at 49% to 46%, and a Hart Research poll at 49% to 45%, summarizing that the contest is virtually deadlocked but with Jackson narrowly ahead in all surveys.

sources.name: UNH Survey Center (Maine Democratic Senate primary preferences)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center release focuses mainly on Democratic primary voters preferring Jackson as the Democratic nominee for Senate, implying his strength within the party but not giving a general-election margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report (statewide Maine PVI)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index rates Maine as D+2, indicating that in recent presidential elections the state has voted about two points more Democratic than the national average.
